diagrams.title: Five Moves Before the First Drawback Claim
diagrams.subtitle: From the five-year lookback to a self-run mock audit
diagrams.caption: Drawback specialists test the opportunity first, then run a shipment trace, clean the export records and stage a mock audit before Customs asks for anything.
diagrams.assumptions_note: The order of steps follows the operator gates and pro-tips the practitioners cited. Customs refunds 99% of eligible duties, taxes and fees and keeps 1%, as International Tariff Management reports.
diagrams.note: Sources are Evana, Scarlett Jones, the Connecticut District Export Council (Jay Charco), the International Trade Council (Tony Nogueiras) and KPMG US.

stages.label: Run the five-year lookback test
stages.detail: First-time claimants can reach back five years from import. Mid-sized companies that assume drawback is only for big companies find the number gets their CFO's attention (Evana).

stages.label: Weigh recovery against filing cost
stages.detail: If projected recovery does not beat the administrative expense of filing, do not file (Scarlett Jones). Specialist fees start around 10% of recovery (Nogueiras).

stages.label: Trace one shipment PO to export
stages.detail: Trace a single shipment from purchase order to import, through inventory and on to export. Customs grants waiver of prior notice off that trace (Connecticut District Export Council).

stages.label: Scrub the export database
stages.detail: Test export records against hard-copy export documents. Remove foreign-to-foreign moves, cancelled orders and short shipments (International Trade Council).

stages.label: Stage a mock desk audit
stages.detail: Know where every record and data element lives before Customs asks. Most Customs checks are spot checks or desk reviews, and companies usually get caught on proof of exportation (KPMG US, International Trade Council).

diagrams.title: Protest Surge Funnel to the 180-Day Clock
diagrams.subtitle: CBP protest volumes narrowing to the filing window that governs every challenge
diagrams.caption: Protest filings rose from about 28,000 a year to 93,000 in 2020. That surge is why CBP's protest team pushes for grouped, well-documented protests filed inside 180 days of liquidation.
diagrams.assumptions_note: The first four stages are protest counts and the last stage is a deadline in days. The figures were reported separately and are not a conversion series. Counts for 2019 and the years before it are approximate, as the speakers gave them.
diagrams.note: Sources are the U.S. Customs and Border Protection protest team for the volumes and FDAImports.com, LLC for the 180-day protest window.

stages.label: Open or suspended protests
stages.detail: Open or suspended protests in CBP's queue when the team reported its numbers.

stages.label: Protests filed in 2020
stages.conversion: Part of the 221 percent increase CBP reported
stages.detail: Lead entry goes first in ACE, with 10-digit HTS plus Chapter 99 numbers.

stages.label: Protests filed in 2019
stages.detail: CBP's stated best practice is to group entries that have similar exclusions.

stages.label: Annual protests before 2019
stages.detail: A further-review request needs a specific because statement.

stages.label: Protest window after liquidation
stages.conversion: After this, the CBP decision is final
stages.detail: After that come 30 days to deemed denial under accelerated disposition, payment of all duties and interest, and a CIT summons within 180 days.

diagrams.title: IEEPA Refund Pipeline Walk
diagrams.subtitle: From the $166B collected to accepted, certified and paid refunds
diagrams.caption: Refunds go only to the importer of record, through CAPE inside ACE, by ACH with interest. Billions remain outside the pipeline or stuck on missing bank details.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Values are in USD billions. Each bar is a separately reported snapshot drawn from CBP court filings, so the bars do not add up exactly. Accepted and certified figures are as of October 2. The paid figure is an earlier snapshot from July 31.
diagrams.note: Sources are Tariffs Lawsuit (Michael Watson), the PolitiClash scoreboard, Finn's Fine Print and Trade Winds Report.

diagrams.title: Drawback Claim Economics in Percent
diagrams.subtitle: Refund rate, unclaimed share, matching uplift and partner incentive
diagrams.caption: Drawback returns 99% of eligible duties, taxes and fees. Most of the pool goes unclaimed, and optimal substitution matching can lift recovery well beyond greedy logic.
diagrams.assumptions_note: All values are percentages reported by the named speakers. Where a speaker gave a single figure, min, max and typical are equal. Section 232, AD/CVD and over-quota duties are excluded from recovery.
diagrams.note: Sources are Thompson Hine LLP (Aaron Mandelbaum), Flexport (Monica Pascarella and the drawback team), USA Customs Clearance and World Trade Center Denver.

diagrams.title: ACE Refund Readiness Gates
diagrams.subtitle: Four checks before a CAPE declaration can pay out by ACH
diagrams.caption: Since February 6, 2026, CBP pays refunds only by ACH to bank details registered in the ACE portal. Each gate below closes a failure point practitioners have seen.
diagrams.assumptions_note: The gate order follows the setup sequence the speakers walked through. CAPE refund speed estimates range from about 3 business days to 60-90 days.
diagrams.note: Sources are Scarbrough Global, Ask The Customs Manager, Shapiro, NextGen CPA, TEU Global and BGI Worldwide Logistics, Inc.

nodes.question: Is the ACE portal account approved and unlocked with the shared secret?
nodes.fail_action: Apply with company and IOR details. Three failed attempts lock the account, and a locked-out TAO calls the ACE helpdesk with the shared secret (Shapiro).

nodes.question: Are routing and account numbers loaded in the ACE portal itself?
nodes.fail_action: Load and double-check bank details. Paying duty by ACH or periodic monthly statement does not register you, and a wrong account sends the refund into the void for months.

nodes.question: Are CF28 and CF29 deliveries switched from mail to portal?
nodes.fail_action: Select portal plus mail delivery. A three-week mail delay can leave as little as 5 days of the 30-day CF28 window (Scarbrough Global).

nodes.question: Is every IEEPA-hit 7501 captured, with its liquidation date tracked?
nodes.fail_action: Pull the ES-001 and ES-003 line-tariff reports from 2025 forward and track the 180-day protest clock. A missed entry means a new declaration at the back of the queue (NextGen CPA).

diagrams.title: The Customs Broker Operating Model
diagrams.subtitle: A licensed agent whose authority comes from a direct POA
diagrams.caption: A broker's authority comes entirely from a properly executed direct power of attorney. The license survives only through demonstrable responsible supervision and control.
diagrams.assumptions_note: CBP sets no staffing ratio and judges each operation case by case, so no headcount is assigned. Fee and exam figures are as the practitioners reported them.
diagrams.note: Sources are CH Powell Company, Braumiller Law Group, PLLC, CONECT Recorded Webinars, Ask The Customs Manager, Steve Fodor, Nadeem Virk and Factory Floor Economics.

center.headcount: No staffing ratio; CBP judges each operation case by case
center.focus: Responsible supervision and control under direct POAs; $150-250 per standard entry and $250-400 for complex work

spokes.kpi: Confirms the broker actually remits duties, because the IOR stays liable if the broker fails to pay
Around $400-500 a year when the bond is bought direct rather than through the broker
72-hour breach reporting; individual license fee raised from $200 to $300
60 of 80 correct in 4.5 hours, open book; classification is the largest section with 15-20 questions

diagrams.title: Bond and AD/CVD Exposure Bands
diagrams.subtitle: From the $50K bond floor to $22M of stacked step-up exposure
diagrams.caption: A bond is a revenue guarantee, not insurance. Size it from rolling 365-day duties, taxes and fees, and skip intermediate sizes rather than stepping up one size at a time.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Values are in USD millions. Bond sufficiency is 10% of annual duties, taxes and fees with a $50K minimum. The AD/CVD bucket uses the single container example the speaker gave.
diagrams.note: Sources are Trade Risk Guaranty for bond sizing and step-up exposure and Ask The Customs Manager for the AD/CVD container example.

buckets.label: Minimum continuous bond
buckets.notes: $50K floor; a $50K bond covers $500K of duties, taxes and fees.

buckets.label: AD/CVD bill on one aluminum container
buckets.notes: A $50K container draws a $150K duty bill; AD/CVD runs 50% to over 300% of value.

buckets.label: Mid-term step-up path
buckets.notes: $5M to $7M to $10M; one-size bumps fail within 12 months nine times out of 10.

buckets.label: Stacked exposure from stepping
buckets.notes: The step-up path stacks $22M; start at $10M or skip $7M instead.

diagrams.title: Settlement Claim Recovery Roadmap
diagrams.subtitle: Verify, recover credentials, document honestly, file and confirm
diagrams.caption: Antitrust and class action money goes only to people who file, and only 4% of eligible consumers do. Each week clears one checkpoint the practitioners flagged.
diagrams.assumptions_note: The weekly sequence organizes the steps practitioners described and is not a deadline any of them stated. Fees come off the top first; about 24% of the $2.8 billion Blue Cross pot goes to plaintiffs' lawyers.
diagrams.note: Sources are News4JAX The Local Station, Crazy Deals and Steals, Receipts, Horty Springer & Mattern, P.C., The Class Action Attorney and NBC4 Washington.

weeks.title: Verify the notice
weeks.deliverable: Official settlement site confirmed; any upfront payment, gift card, crypto or Social Security number request refused
weeks.gate: No payment requested, because real claims carry no administrative charge

weeks.title: Recover claim credentials
weeks.deliverable: Unique ID and PIN recovered by searching email for the administrator name, such as Kroll on AT&T, or through the resend page
weeks.gate: A working ID and PIN in hand

weeks.title: Build honest counts and proof
weeks.deliverable: Fee counts built from old bank statements; Option B Blue Cross filers attach Excel spreadsheets of allowed amounts
weeks.gate: Estimates that hold up under penalty of perjury

weeks.title: File with proof and confirm payout
weeks.deliverable: Claim filed with uploaded proof toward caps like the $7,500 AT&T ceiling; middleman fees weighed against free filing
weeks.gate: Administrator confirms any unexpected check before it is cashed
